## What's new in 1.3.1

Everything from 1.3.0, plus the Linux video calls from 1.1.1.

- **Video calls from Linux.** The Linux PC and Raspberry Pi desktop apps can now send their camera too, not just show video. During a call, press **Camera on**. The camera menu next to it lists the built-in webcam and any USB webcam, so you can choose one.
  - Like on Android and Windows, the camera never turns on by itself: every call starts with it off, and it turns off when the call ends.
  - Webcams that offer MJPEG send their pictures as they are, so it barely uses the CPU (good for a Raspberry Pi). Others are converted and compressed on the fly.
  - Video is end-to-end encrypted like the rest of the call.
  - Your user needs access to the camera (`/dev/video*`). Desktop logins normally have it; otherwise run `sudo usermod -aG video $USER` and log in again. If the camera is busy in another app, the app says so.
- Also included from 1.3.0 and 1.2.0: the **Linux system tray icon**, **encrypted calls** with a security code, and the optional **intercom password**.

Upgrading: install over 1.2.0 or 1.3.0 (same variant on Android). Settings and saved peers are kept. 1.3.1 works with 1.2.0 and 1.3.0; versions before 1.2.0 (including 1.1.1) can't connect, because they don't encrypt.
